federal.name: Government of Pakistan
federal.desc: Federal executive branch headed by the Prime Minister, organized into roughly 32 ministries and 39 divisions under the Cabinet. Coordinates national policy in areas the Constitution reserves to the centre — defence, foreign affairs, currency, and matters on the Federal Legislative List — while most service-delivery functions were devolved to the provinces after the 18th Amendment (2010).

children.name: Cabinet Secretariat
children.desc: Apex coordinating body of the federal government, comprising five divisions that service the Cabinet and the Prime Minister's Office directly. Its Cabinet Division prepares Cabinet agendas and circulates decisions to every ministry for implementation.

children.name: Aviation Division
children.desc: Sets civil aviation policy and oversees the Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority and national carrier matters. Handles international air-service agreements and airport regulation.

children.name: Cabinet Division
children.desc: Provides secretarial support to the federal Cabinet and its committees. Also houses several attached departments including the Federal Public Service Commission's administrative liaison.

children.name: Establishment Division
children.desc: Manages the federal civil service: recruitment rules, postings, training and service structure for the Pakistan Administrative Service and other federal cadres. Works closely with the Federal Public Service Commission on entry-level recruitment.

children.name: National Security Division
children.desc: Coordinates national security policy across military and civilian institutions. A relatively recent addition to the Cabinet Secretariat, formalizing what was previously ad hoc coordination.

children.name: Poverty Alleviation & Social Safety Division
children.desc: Federal policy home for cash-transfer and safety-net programs, including oversight of BISP. Coordinates with provincial social-welfare and zakat/baitulmaal departments on beneficiary targeting.

children.name: Ministries / Divisions
children.desc: The bulk of federal executive authority, organized into ministries (political heads) split further into divisions (administrative units), each headed by a Secretary. The exact count shifts with every cabinet reorganization.

children.name: Finance & Revenue
children.desc: Combines the Finance Division (federal budget, borrowing, NFC award distribution to provinces) and the Revenue Division (tax policy, oversight of FBR). The NFC award is the main channel through which federal revenue reaches Punjab's own Finance Department.

children.name: Interior
children.desc: Federal internal security ministry overseeing NADRA, FIA, and the Islamabad Capital Territory administration. Coordinates with provincial Home Departments on law-and-order matters that cross provincial lines.

children.name: Foreign Affairs
children.desc: Conducts Pakistan's diplomacy and represents the federation in international bodies. Provinces have no independent foreign-affairs role under the Constitution.

children.name: Defence / Defence Production
children.desc: Administers the armed forces and the domestic defence-industrial base across two divisions. An exclusively federal subject under the Constitution.

children.name: Planning, Development & Special Initiatives
children.desc: Federal counterpart to Punjab's Planning & Development Board; sets national five-year plans and approves large development schemes through the Central Development Working Party. Provincial P&D departments submit PC-1 project documents up through this ministry for federally-funded schemes.

children.name: Commerce
children.desc: Sets national trade policy, tariffs and export strategy. Works with provincial Industries departments on regional export-processing initiatives.

children.name: Energy (Power + Petroleum)
children.desc: Two divisions covering the national power grid and petroleum sector respectively; oversees WAPDA, NEPRA and OGRA. Provincial energy companies like QATPL and PTPL sell power into the national grid regulated from here.

children.name: National Health Services
children.desc: Federal health ministry responsible for national disease-control programs, drug regulation (DRAP) and international health coordination, since service delivery itself was devolved to provincial health departments in 2011.

children.name: Federal Education & Heritage
children.desc: Covers professional training, national heritage and culture, plus a residual federal role in curriculum standards even though school education itself is a provincial subject. Houses the Higher Education Commission's parent portfolio.

children.name: IT & Telecommunication
leads: Shaza Fatima Khawaja, Federal Minister (since Mar 2024)
children.desc: Sets national digital policy and telecom regulation through PTA; runs the Digital Pakistan initiative. Coordinates with provincial IT boards — including Punjab's PITB — on shared e-governance standards, though each provincial board reports administratively to its own province.
children.related: Coordinates with provincial IT boards on digital-governance standards

children.name: Water Resources
leads: Muhammad Moeen Wattoo, Federal Minister (since Mar 2025)
children.desc: Oversees WAPDA and inter-provincial water-sharing arrangements under the 1991 Water Apportionment Accord. Provincial Irrigation departments operate the canal network that WAPDA's barrages feed.

children.name: Law & Justice
children.desc: Federal legal affairs, drafting of federal legislation, and liaison with the superior judiciary. Distinct from each province's own Law & Parliamentary Affairs department.

children.name: Other ministries
children.desc: The remaining federal ministries, each a full portfolio in its own right. Expand to see each one individually.

children.name: Climate Change
children.desc: National climate policy and adaptation strategy, an increasingly prominent portfolio after the 2022 floods.

children.name: Communications
children.desc: Oversees the National Highway Authority and federal road infrastructure.

children.name: Human Rights
children.desc: Federal human-rights policy and treaty-body reporting.

children.name: Industries & Production
children.desc: Industrial policy for federally-regulated heavy industry and state-owned manufacturing.

children.name: Information & Broadcasting
children.desc: Federal media policy; parent ministry for PEMRA.

children.name: Inter-Provincial Coordination
children.desc: Facilitates coordination between federal and provincial governments, including the Council of Common Interests secretariat.

children.name: Kashmir Affairs & Gilgit-Baltistan
children.desc: Administers federal relations with Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, both outside the standard provincial structure.

children.name: Maritime Affairs
children.desc: Ports, shipping and maritime policy, including the Karachi and Gwadar port authorities.

children.name: Narcotics Control
children.desc: Federal narcotics enforcement policy, currently held jointly with the Interior portfolio.

children.name: National Food Security & Research
children.desc: Federal agricultural research and food-security policy, distinct from each province's own agriculture department.

children.name: Overseas Pakistanis & HR Development
children.desc: Emigrant welfare and remittance-linked policy; runs the overseas employment bureaus.

children.name: Parliamentary Affairs
children.desc: Manages government business in the National Assembly and Senate.

children.name: Privatisation
children.desc: Runs the Privatisation Commission's divestment program for state-owned enterprises.

children.name: Railways
children.desc: Operates Pakistan Railways, one of the largest state-owned enterprises.

children.name: Religious Affairs & Interfaith Harmony
children.desc: Manages Hajj arrangements and federal religious-affairs policy.

children.name: States & Frontier Regions
children.desc: Administers federally-administered areas and frontier-region affairs.

children.name: Science & Technology
children.desc: Federal science policy, distinct from the IT & Telecom portfolio.

children.name: Housing & Works
children.desc: Federal government buildings and housing schemes, including the Federal Government Employees Housing Foundation.

children.name: Major attached bodies & regulators
children.desc: Autonomous or semi-autonomous agencies that sit administratively under a parent ministry but operate with their own statutory mandate and, usually, their own board.

children.name: Federal Board of Revenue
children.desc: Collects federal taxes — income tax, customs duty, and sales tax on goods — under the Revenue Division. Sales tax on services was devolved to the provinces in 2011, which is why Punjab collects its own through PRA.
children.related: Shares tax-jurisdiction boundaries with Punjab's own revenue authority

children.name: State Bank of Pakistan
children.desc: Pakistan's independent central bank, responsible for monetary policy, currency issuance and banking-sector supervision. Regulates the Bank of Punjab as a scheduled commercial bank alongside every other bank in the country.

children.name: Securities & Exchange Commission
children.desc: Regulates capital markets, corporate registration and non-bank financial companies nationwide, under the Finance Division. All Section-42 provincial companies (like PSDF or PMDFC) are registered and regulated by SECP.

children.name: National Database & Registration Authority
children.desc: Issues the national CNIC and maintains Pakistan's civil registry, under the Ministry of Interior. Its identity data underpins most provincial e-governance and welfare-verification systems, including Punjab's own service portals.

children.name: Federal Investigation Agency
children.desc: Investigates federal crimes — immigration, cybercrime, financial fraud spanning provincial borders — under the Ministry of Interior. Works alongside provincial police and Punjab's Anti-Corruption Establishment on overlapping cases.

children.name: Pakistan Telecommunication Authority
children.desc: Regulates telecom operators, spectrum allocation and internet policy nationwide, under the IT & Telecom Division. A purely federal subject; provinces have no independent telecom-licensing power.

children.name: Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority
children.desc: Licenses and regulates private TV and radio broadcasters nationwide, under Information & Broadcasting. Provincial Information departments run their own public messaging but cannot license broadcasters.

children.name: National Disaster Management Authority
leads: Lt Gen Inam Haider Malik, Chairman (since Oct 2022)
children.desc: Coordinates national disaster response and sits under the Prime Minister's Office; established after the 2005 earthquake exposed gaps in disaster coordination. Works directly with each province's PDMA during major floods and emergencies.
children.related: Coordinates directly with Punjab's Provincial Disaster Management Authority during emergencies

children.name: Higher Education Commission
leads: Prof. Dr. Niaz Ahmad Akhtar, Chairman (since Feb 2026)
children.desc: Sets national higher-education standards, accredits degree programs and disburses federal research funding to universities. Provincial higher-education commissions, including Punjab's PHEC, apply HEC's accreditation framework locally.
children.related: Provincial higher-education commissions apply HEC's national accreditation standards

children.name: National Accountability Bureau
children.desc: Investigates and prosecutes corruption cases above certain financial thresholds, reporting to the President/PM. Its jurisdiction can overlap with Punjab's Anti-Corruption Establishment on major provincial cases.

children.name: Benazir Income Support Programme
children.desc: Pakistan's largest unconditional cash-transfer program, under the Poverty Alleviation & Social Safety Division. Coordinates beneficiary lists with provincial welfare bodies like Punjab's Bait-ul-Maal to avoid duplicate support.
children.related: Coordinates beneficiary data with Punjab's Bait-ul-Maal welfare programs

children.name: Water & Power Development Authority
leads: Lt Gen (Retd) Muhammad Saeed, Chairman (since Aug 2025)
children.desc: Builds and operates major dams, barrages and the national transmission grid, under the Water Resources Division. Feeds the canal network that Punjab's own Irrigation Department distributes to farmland.
children.related: Feeds the barrage/canal system that Punjab's Irrigation Department distributes locally

children.name: Federal Public Service Commission
children.desc: Recruits into federal civil-service posts through competitive exam, linked to the Establishment Division. Its provincial counterpart, the PPSC, runs an entirely separate recruitment process for Punjab government posts.

children.name: Capital Development Authority
children.desc: Plans and governs Islamabad, the federal capital, functioning much like a provincial development authority but reporting to the Ministry of Interior/Cabinet instead of a province.

provincial.name: Government of the Punjab
leads: Maryam Nawaz Sharif — Chief Minister (since 26 Feb 2024)
Sardar Saleem Haider Khan — Governor (since 1 May 2024)
provincial.desc: Provincial executive branch headed by the Chief Minister, running 46 Civil Secretariat departments plus a separately-elected local-government tier. Holds autonomous, devolved authority under the 18th Amendment (2010) over subjects like health, education, agriculture and local government — these are not federal responsibilities delegated downward, but powers the province holds constitutionally in its own right.

children.name: Civil Secretariat departments
children.desc: The 46 top administrative units of the Punjab government, each headed by a Secretary reporting through the Chief Secretary to the Chief Minister. Every attached department, authority and company below ultimately sits under one of these. The count moves as departments are split or merged — the Office of AI's own stock-take puts the current working figure at 46.

children.name: Additional Chief Secretary Office
children.desc: Supports the Chief Secretary in coordinating across departments; distinct from the Chief Secretary's own office, which sits outside the 42 line departments as an oversight function.

children.name: Board of Revenue
children.desc: The senior-most department in Punjab's administrative hierarchy, responsible for land revenue, land records and the district revenue bureaucracy (patwaris, tehsildars) that predates independence. Its head, the Senior Member Board of Revenue, ranks among the most senior civil servants in the province.

children.name: Punjab Land Records Authority
children.desc: Runs the computerized land-record system launched in 2017, replacing the colonial-era patwari registers with digital records accessible online. One of Pakistan's more widely cited e-governance success stories.

children.name: Directorate of Land Records
children.desc: Attached department responsible for maintaining physical land records ahead of full digitization, and for legacy record disputes that predate the PLRA system.

children.name: Finance Department
children.desc: Prepares the provincial budget, manages public expenditure, and receives Punjab's share of the federal divisible pool under the NFC award. The largest single lever of provincial policy, since every department's spending runs through it.

children.name: Punjab Revenue Authority
children.desc: Collects sales tax on services within Punjab, a tax category devolved to the provinces in 2011 after the 18th Amendment. Operates alongside, not under, the federal FBR, which retains sales tax on goods.
children.related: Operates the services-tax jurisdiction devolved from FBR after the 18th Amendment

children.name: Bank of Punjab
children.desc: A government-owned scheduled commercial bank in which Punjab holds a controlling stake of roughly 57.5 percent as of end-2024. Regulated like any other bank by the federal State Bank of Pakistan.

children.name: Inspectorate of Treasuries and Accounts
children.desc: Inspects district treasuries and departmental accounts for the Finance Department, checking expenditure and reconciliation before the Accountant General's formal audit trail.

Pensions Direct Credit System for pension processing/disbursement

Life Certificate administration via bank branches

children.desc: Regulates planned development and building control across Lahore. Contains WASA Lahore and TEPA as operating wings rather than separate legal entities.

children.addr: 8th Floor, Tower C, Old P&D Building, Lahore (also listed: 27-Shadman II, Jail Road, Lahore)

children.name: Department of Tourist Services
children.desc: Registers and regulates hotels, travel agents and tour operators under the Pakistan Hotels and Restaurants Act.
children.head: Socrat Aman Mana, Secretary, Department of Tourist Services, Punjab
wings: Punjab Tourism Squad (PTS) - led by Assistant Director Operations Syed Khurram Hasan
services: DTS Online Registration and License Portal (hotels, restaurants, travel agencies)
eBiz Punjab Portal for new registrations/licenses
Regulation and enforcement of hospitality standards
Magnificent Punjab tourism promotion (170 priority sites mapped)

children.name: Punjab Tourism for Economic Growth
children.desc: World Bank-supported programme developing tourism infrastructure and destination management as an economic-growth strategy.
wings: Youth Affairs, Sports, Archeology and Tourism Department (YASA&T)
services: Institutional development / tourism policy reform support
Infrastructure development at eight heritage sites
Private sector engagement for job creation
children.addr: 175-A, Scotch Corner, Upper Mall Scheme, Lahore

children.name: Chief Minister's Secretariat & oversight
children.desc: The Chief Minister's own office and the monitoring, inspection and reform units that report to her directly rather than through a line department. These bodies cut across the Secretariat: they inspect other departments, chase project delivery and run the CM's special initiatives.

children.name: Office of the Chief Minister of Punjab
children.desc: The Chief Minister's principal secretariat at 8-Club Road, GOR-I. Coordinates cabinet business, runs the CM's flagship initiatives and directs the Chief Secretary on execution across all forty-odd departments.
children.head: Ms. Maryam Nawaz Sharif, Chief Minister of Punjab (since Feb 26, 2024)
services: Nine focus areas: Youth/e-commerce connectivity, Local Government, Environment/climate, Culture, Women's Rights, Agriculture, Law & Order, Education, Healthcare

children.name: Chief Minister's Inspection Team
children.desc: Inspects development schemes and departmental administration on the Chief Minister's instruction, and handles complaints routed from the CM's office, NAB and the public. Reports findings upward rather than to the department being inspected.
services: Administrative oversight and policy implementation monitoring
Handling complaints (CM directives, NAB complaints, departmental complaints, public complaints, mega project inspections)
children.addr: Prof. Ashfaq Ali Khan Road, Anarkali Bazaar, Lahore

children.name: Chief Minister's Special Monitoring Unit
children.desc: A small analytics and delivery unit tracking progress on the Chief Minister's priority programmes, using dashboards and field verification rather than departmental self-reporting.
services: Monitoring of education initiatives (laptop schemes, internships, scholarships)
Healthcare monitoring (free medicine programs, clinics on wheels, field hospitals)

children.name: Punjab Overseas Pakistanis Commission
children.desc: Hears and resolves complaints from overseas Pakistanis — mostly property, land-record and inheritance disputes — through district committees in 23 districts and international e-Khuli Kachehri sessions.
children.head: Barrister Amjad Malik (Vice Chairperson)
services: Khuli Kachehri and International e-Khuli Kachehri sessions
Property/land record verification and dispute assistance
Community engagement with overseas Pakistanis and diplomatic missions

children.name: Boutique Resorts Punjab
children.desc: Runs the provincial government's guest properties in the Murree hills — Government House Murree, Punjab House Murree and the Bhurban forest rest house — as bookable accommodation.
services: Luxury accommodation booking and reservations at Murree Hills properties
Guest amenities (24/7 hot water, heating, security, staff support)

children.name: Governor's House Lahore
children.desc: The Governor is the constitutional head of the province, appointed by the President on the Prime Minister's advice. The role is largely ceremonial after the 18th Amendment — assent to provincial legislation, oath-taking, and chancellorship of public universities — with executive power resting with the Chief Minister.
children.head: Sardar Saleem Haider Khan, Governor of Punjab (took oath May 1, 2024)
services: General public visits/tours of the historic residence
children.addr: Governor House Punjab, The Mall Road, Lahore

children.name: Local government tier
children.desc: A legally separate, elected tier of government under the Punjab Local Government Act 2019/2022 — administratively linked to LG&CD but not one of its subordinate offices. Mayoral and council seats have been vacant since December 2021, with administrators running affairs pending fresh local elections.

children.name: Metropolitan Corporations
children.desc: The top urban tier: Lahore, Faisalabad, Rawalpindi, Multan, Gujranwala, Bahawalpur, Sargodha, Sahiwal and Dera Ghazi Khan, each meeting the population threshold for metropolitan status.

children.name: Metropolitan Corporation Lahore
children.desc: Lahore's metropolitan corporation — the elected municipal tier for the city, distinct from LDA (development control) and WASA (utilities).
wings: Core Team/leadership section referenced (not detailed on fetched page)
services: Chief Minister's Lahore Development Plan initiatives

children.name: Municipal Corporations
children.desc: Second-tier cities above the standard municipality population threshold but below metropolitan scale.

children.name: Municipal Committees
children.desc: Smaller urban local councils covering most of Punjab's mid-sized towns.

children.name: Town Committees
children.desc: The smallest urban local-government tier, for the province's smaller towns.

children.name: Tehsil Councils
children.desc: The rural local-government tier below district level, covering areas outside municipal boundaries.

children.name: Union / Neighbourhood Councils
children.desc: The lowest tier of local government, intended as the grassroots representative body closest to citizens.

children.name: District Administration
children.desc: A parallel, non-elected bureaucratic tier under the Punjab Civil Administration Act 2017, headed by a Deputy Commissioner — legally distinct from the elected local-government bodies above even though both operate at similar geographic scale.

children.name: Punjab Public Service Commission
children.desc: Recruits into provincial civil-service posts through competitive examination, established in 1937 and re-constituted by a 1978 Ordinance. A constitutional body reporting to the Governor rather than to any single department, running a recruitment process entirely separate from the federal FPSC.

children.name: Judiciary, tribunals & watchdogs
children.desc: Bodies that sit outside the executive chain of command. The High Court and its academy belong to the judicial branch; the Ombudsman offices, Information Commission and appellate tribunals are quasi-judicial watchdogs that hear complaints against government departments rather than report to them.

children.name: Lahore High Court
children.desc: The provincial superior court, with principal seat in Lahore and benches at Rawalpindi, Multan and Bahawalpur. Constitutionally independent of the provincial executive; the Law & Parliamentary Affairs Department handles liaison, not supervision.
children.head: Miss Aalia Neelum, Chief Justice (per site content referencing a June 2026 press release; verify current officeholder)
services: Cause lists and hearing status updates

children.name: Lahore High Court Museum
children.desc: Heritage museum inside the High Court building, founded by Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah, documenting the court's colonial-era architecture and judicial history.
children.head: Founded by Justice Syed Mansoor Ali Shah; currently overseen by Monitoring Judge Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan (no single 'Director' named)
services: Preservation and display of LHC's legal/historical heritage

children.name: Punjab Judicial Academy
children.desc: Trains judicial officers and court staff for the province. Chaired ex-officio by the Chief Justice of the Lahore High Court, which keeps it inside the judicial branch rather than the executive.
children.head: Chairperson: Chief Justice Miss Aalia Neelum; Director General: Mr. Justice (R) Sardar Ahmad Naeem

children.name: Punjab Judicial Academy Law Journal
children.desc: The Academy's peer-reviewed law journal, published under a board of management chaired by the Chief Justice.
children.head: Hon'ble Chief Justice of Lahore High Court (Chairperson, Board of Management); Director General, PJA manages operations
wings: Board of Management (includes two LHC judges, Registrar, a District & Sessions Judge, govt secretaries, Principal of Punjab University Law College)
services: Punjab Judicial Academy Law Journal (peer-reviewed, open access, biannual, English/Urdu)
Judicial and court staff training programs

children.name: Office of the Ombudsman Punjab
children.desc: Investigates maladministration complaints against provincial government agencies and can direct remedial action. Free to approach and outside the department's own grievance chain.

children.name: Office of the Ombudsperson Punjab
children.desc: A separate office handling workplace-harassment complaints under the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act 2010, distinct from the general Ombudsman.
children.head: Dr. Najma Afzal Khan, 5th Ombudsperson Punjab (assumed charge April 8, 2026)
wings: Eight regional offices: Gujrat, Gujranwala, Rawalpindi, Bahawalpur, Dera Ghazi Khan, Multan, Sargodha, Sahiwal
services: Administers Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010
Administers Punjab Enforcement of Women's Property Rights Act, 2021
Complaint management and tracking system / mobile app for grievance filing
FAQs, forms, guidelines, hearing schedules, published decisions, annual reports

children.name: Punjab Information Commission
children.desc: Enforces the Punjab Transparency and Right to Information Act — hears appeals when a department refuses an information request, and can penalise Public Information Officers for non-compliance.
wings: Public Information Officers (PIOs) network across govt departments
services: RTI application filing and complaint handling
FAQs and sample RTI application templates

children.name: Appellate Tribunal Punjab Revenue Authority
children.desc: Hears appeals against sales-tax-on-services assessments made by the Punjab Revenue Authority. Sits above PRA's internal appeal process, below the High Court.
services: Appeals management for sales tax on services disputes
Case documentation, cause lists and judgements
children.addr: Shadman-II, Lahore (site lists: 192, Abu Bakar Block, New Garden Town, Lahore)

children.name: Punjab Charity Commission
children.desc: Registers and monitors charities, NGOs, trusts and societies under the Punjab Charities Act 2018, and runs the public charity-search register donors use to verify an organisation.
services: Charity registration portal for NPOs, NGOs, charities, trusts, societies (Punjab Charities Act 2018)
Video tutorials, user guides, FAQs for applicants
children.addr: Punjab Civil Secretariat, Lower Mall, Lahore
